items.title: Easterly winds set to end Telangana’s cold nights
points: The ongoing spell of chilly nights across Telangana is likely to ease over the next few days as easterly winds begin to replace the cold northerly winds currently influencing the region.
Meteorologists at the Telangana Development Planning Society (TGDPS) also expect the remainder of the winter season to be relatively mild, also due to the impact of El Nino conditions.

Hyderabad and surrounding areas have been recording night temperatures between 15°C and 18°C, while districts are witnessing readings ranging from 14°C to 19°C under the influence of cool northerly winds.
If conditions remain favourable, it could bring light rainfall to parts of south Telangana for one or two days around November 19-20.
The State recorded a rainfall deficit of 86% in October but Mr. Rao noted that deficient October rainfall has become increasingly common in recent years and is not unique to 2026.
The northeast monsoon, which normally contributes about 11 cm of rainfall by December, has delivered only 3 cm so far, a deficit of nearly 70%.

items.title: Uttam slams BRS for using drought as a political tool
points: Uttam Kumar Reddy on Wednesday accused the BRS of exploiting drought conditions for political gain and spreading false allegations that Telangana’s share of Krishna and Godavari waters was being diverted to Andhra Pradesh.

He said the Congress government had utilised more water from both rivers since assuming office in December 2023 and achieved higher agricultural acreage, paddy production and procurement compared to the BRS regime.

Speaking during inspections of irrigation projects and the Young India Integrated Residential School in Suryapet district, Mr. Uttam Kumar Reddy said the allegations were baseless and aimed at misleading farmers.

He claimed the government had paid nearly ₹90,000 crore to paddy farmers through procurement operations, with payments credited within 48 hours, and highlighted the ₹500-per-quintal bonus for fine varieties of paddy.
The Minister alleged that the BRS leadership was attempting to capitalise on drought conditions caused by El Niño instead of supporting farmers.

items.title: Cabinet approves ₹3,230-crore project to develop Yug Yugeen Bharat Museum
points: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, on Wednesday (November 11, 2026), approved a 3,230-crore project to develop the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum in the historic North and South Block buildings in New Delhi.
The proposal was appraised by the Public Investment Board (PIB) on 27 July 2026, and the Ministry of Culture has concurred with its recommendations.
The museum, announced by the Prime Minister on 18 May 2023, will showcase India’s civilisational journey and its tangible and intangible cultural heritage.

It will be developed by adaptively reusing the historic North and South Block Complex, preserving their architectural character and heritage significance while transforming them into a public cultural institution.
Spread over a proposed built-up area of approximately 1,78,509 square metres, the museum will integrate contemporary museum practices, immersive technologies and visitor-centric interpretation.
The project will be implemented in phases between the 2026-27 and 2030-31 financial years.

items.title: Gorakhpur-bound train derails at Kanpur Central, four coaches go off tracks; no casualties
points: Four coaches of the Chauri Chaura Express derailed while the train was departing from Kanpur Central railway station in Uttar Pradesh on Wednesday evening.
Train number 15003, travelling from Kanpur Anwarganj to Gorakhpur, arrived at Platform 7 and departed at 5.03 pm.
Around two minutes later, as the train was moving out of the station, coaches B4, B5, B6 and B7 derailed.
Deputy chief traffic manager (CTM), Kanpur Central, Akshanshu Govil said around 300 passengers were travelling in the four affected coaches and all were safe.

The derailment comes hours after another train accident in Assam, where six passenger coaches and the locomotive of the Kolkata-Sairang Express derailed at Digaru railway station on the outskirts of Guwahati early Wednesday morning.

While the Northeast Frontier Railway initially said there were no reports of casualties, Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma later said four people had sustained minor injuries and were receiving medical care.

items.title: Ex-Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar Collapses During Walk, Hospitalised
points: Former vice president Jagdeep Dhankhar was admitted to AIIMS here on Wednesday after he fell unconscious during his morning walk, sources said.

The 75-year-old former Rajya Sabha chairman has been admitted to the hospital's cardio-neuro centre and is currently under the care of the department of cardiology for medical evaluation and treatment, the sources said.
Security personnel accompanying Dhankhar took him home in a PCR vehicle after he collapsed during the morning walk and remained unconscious for a few minutes.
Dhankhar served as India's 14th vice president from August 2022 until his resignation on July 21, 2025.
In March 2025, he was admitted to AIIMS's critical care unit following chest pain and underwent angioplasty.
During an official visit to Nainital in June 2025, Dhankhar fainted while attending the golden jubilee celebrations of Kumaon University.
He appeared to lose consciousness while embracing former parliamentary colleague Mahendra Singh Pal.
After vacating Uprashtrapati Bhavan, he has been residing at the South Delhi farmhouse of Haryana politician Abhay Choutala.

items.title: Tasmac introduces three year transfer norm for liquor shop employees in Tamil Nadu
points: Lakshmi Narayanan The Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation (Tasmac) is set to reshuffle employees across its retail network in Tamil Nadu, deploying staff at outlets based on manpower requirements.
Under a new Transfer and Posting Policy for Tasmac liquor Retail Vending Shop Personnel, 2026, the state run liquor retailer has proposed transferring employees across shops once every three years.
Outlets with average monthly sales of ₹10 lakh and above will be classified as Category A and will have a minimum workforce of nine employees.
Those with sales of more than ₹5 lakh but less than ₹10 lakh will fall under Category B, with a workforce of eight employees.
Outlets recording sales of less than ₹5 lakh will be classified as Category C and will have five employees.
Employees who have complete three years at a shop as on November 1 will be considered for the transfer.

items.title: 6 Crew Missing As Thai Fuel Supply Vessel Sinks Off Sattahip In Gulf Of Thailand
points: The Royal Thai Navy is searching for 6 missing crew members after a fishing fuel-supply vessel, Venus 14, sank in the Gulf of Thailand off the coast of Sattahip.

As per the navy, the Venus 14 went down about 27 nautical miles from the entrance of the channel leading to the Sattahip Naval Base, on bearing 227 degrees, and the alert reached the navy at around 9:00 a.m. on Wednesday, November 11.
The Thai-registered vessel’s fuel load is not known, and neither is the reason behind the sinking.
Nothing has been shared by the navy on the condition or whereabouts of the crew, till now.
On receiving the alert, the First Naval Area Command immediately deployed the patrol boat Tor 113 and a maritime surveillance aircraft, which are tasked with locating the crew and the wreck.
Ships in the vicinity have been asked to exercise caution through a navigational warning.

points: INS Chilka, the Indian Navy’s premier ab initio training establishment in Odisha, India, is set to see more than 3,300 trainees pass out on November 13, the largest batch ever to do so from the establishment, officials said.
This is the Indian Navy’s ninth Agniveer batch.
Indian Coast Guard Naviks are passing out too.
Indian Navy Chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan would review the parade as the chief guest.
Newly recruited Indian Navy sailors and Indian Coast Guard Naviks do their first training here, as per the Navy.
The first batch of Indian Navy Agniveers began training there in November 2022, and 2,585 of them passed out on March 28, 2023, after 16 weeks of training.
Agniveers are youth recruited into the Indian Army, Navy and Air Force under the Agnipath scheme, which the Indian government announced on June 14, 2022.

points: Iran has claimed a strike on Didamar, a small rocky island belonging to Oman at the entrance to the Persian Gulf, according to reports on Tuesday.

items.title: Sea Robbery Incidents in the Straits of Malacca and Singapore
points: Following a significant decline in incidents over the past ten months, there has been a recent spike in reported sea robbery incidents onboard ships while underway in the Singapore Strait.

Three incidents of sea robbery were reported on board ships transiting the eastbound lane of the Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS) in the Straits of Malacca and Singapore (SOMS) on 2, 4, and 10 November 2026.
The first incident occurred on 2 November at 2125 hrs, the second on 4 November at 2335 hrs, and the third on 10 November at 0240 hrs.
All three incidents took place in close proximity to one another (approximately 3.2 nautical miles apart), with two occurring on board bulk carriers and one onboard a tanker.

The port’s methanol bunkering infrastructure comprises an onshore storage facility, connected to a jetty, through a 2.8-km pipeline for shore-to-ship fuel transfers.

items.title: Iron Ore Slides on Expected Steel Production Cuts
points: Iron ore futures slipped toward CNY 680 per ton on Wednesday, reaching a one-week low as expectations of production restrictions across major steelmaking hubs in China’s Hebei province weighed on demand prospects.

Key steel-producing cities, including Tangshan and Handan, have entered the autumn-winter air pollution control period, during which unfavorable weather conditions have periodically disrupted sintering operations and blast furnace utilization.
Expectations are growing that broader production restrictions could be introduced across Hebei, potentially placing further pressure on steel output.
Industry data also showed that average hot metal production among Chinese steelmakers, a key indicator of iron ore demand, continued to decline.

items.title: Copper Rebounds on Tightening Supply in China
points: Copper futures climbed toward $6.30 per pound on Wednesday, recovering from four-month lows amid tightening physical supply in China, the world’s largest copper consumer.

Import premiums in the country have reached record levels in recent weeks, while refined copper shipments have declined this year and domestic smelters have reduced production due to rising ore costs and weaker profit margins.
China has also faced difficulties replenishing its inventories as substantial volumes of copper have been redirected to the US ahead of potential import tariffs.
Additional support came from renewed investor interest in the artificial intelligence sector following strong earnings from neocloud provider CoreWeave.
Copper benefits directly from the global expansion of AI infrastructure due to its essential role in data centers and power networks.

items.title: API Reports Larger-Than-Expected Drop in US Crude Inventories
points: In a surprising development, the American Petroleum Institute (API) has reported a significant decline in US crude oil inventories, signaling stronger-than-anticipated demand in the market.
The latest data shows that crude inventories fell by 9.8 million barrels, a figure that notably surpasses market expectations.
Analysts had forecasted a more moderate reduction in crude stockpiles, anticipating a smaller drawdown.
The actual figure of a 9.8 million barrel decrease starkly contrasts with these predictions, suggesting a robust demand for crude oil that was not fully anticipated by market observers.
This substantial drop in inventories also marks a considerable change from the previous week’s data, where crude stocks had decreased by 5.267 million barrels.
The current drawdown nearly doubles the prior reduction, indicating an acceleration in the consumption of crude oil over the past week.
A larger-than-expected decline in inventories typically suggests heightened demand, which can exert upward pressure on crude oil prices.

items.title: UK taps Ocean Infinity for subsea security push
points: UK-based marine robotics specialist Ocean Infinity has been selected as the Royal Navy’s commercial mission partner for a new underwater surveillance programme backed by an initial £90m ($120m) investment.

The company will work with the Royal Navy to develop Atlantic Net, a network of autonomous maritime systems, underwater sensors and artificial intelligence designed to monitor the North Atlantic and protect critical subsea infrastructure.
The programme forms the first operational phase of the Royal Navy’s wider Atlantic Bastion initiative, which aims to combine crewed warships with autonomous and remotely operated systems.
Atlantic Net will focus on identifying submarine activity and threats to underwater communications cables and energy networks, including in the strategically important Greenland-Iceland-UK gap.
The Ministry of Defence said the framework agreement with Ocean Infinity would pave the way for the £90m investment and support almost 200 skilled jobs.
The system is expected to become operational in 2027, providing Royal Navy warships and Astute-class submarines with earlier warnings of potential underwater threats.
